report.math_notes: Checked line by line. Lemma A (reduction to m_i' = lcm of the gcds): (1) m_i' ≥ 2 because every g_ij ≥ 2 by (*); m_i' | m_i and m_i' | L_k since each g_ij ≤ k-1. (2) g_ij | gcd(m_i',m_j') | gcd(m_i,m_j) = g_ij — correct. (3) a_i' ≡ a_i (mod g_ij) since g_ij | m_i', so g_ij ∤ a_i'-a_j' and (*) gives disjointness — correct. (4) v_p(m_i') = max_j v_p(g_ij) gives the prime-power rule — correct. Lemma B (density criterion): the M/d_i translates a_i + t m_i are pairwise incongruent mod M (gcd(M/d_i, m_i/d_i)=1); if Σ M/d_i > M, pigeonhole gives a_i + t m_i ≡ a_j + s m_j (mod M) with i ≠ j, and g_ij | m_i, m_j, M forces g_ij | a_i - a_j, contradicting (*). Correct, and valid for every sub-family with any common multiple M of that sub-family's gcds; applying it to prefixes of the sorted tuple (incremental pruning) and to all sub-multisets at leaves is therefore sound. Lemma C trivial. Corollary D correctly reduces existence of a counterexample to a non-decreasing tuple in S_k satisfying (R1)–(R3),(R5); no minimality of k is used. Code_1 logic inspected: L = lcm(1..k-1), candidates = divisors ≥ 2, R1 with threshold k-1, incremental R2 over all M | L with lcm(gcds) | M (the size-1 prefix check is vacuous, so no wrong pruning), leaf R3 on maximal prime powers (sufficient by Lemma A(4)) and R2 on all sub-multisets; exact integer arithmetic only. Hence zero stage-A survivors at a size k is a valid proof of the statement at k. The k=13 hand argument for the part (10,10,10,10,10,12,45) is correct (five classes mod 10 distinct mod 10; either they cover Z/5 and meet the 45-class via gcd 5, or two agree mod 5 with opposite parity and one meets the 12-class via gcd 2), so k=13 also follows from the single-survivor output. The optional rules M4/M5 are proved correctly under the stated hypotheses but are not used for any claim. DEPENDENCY EXPOSED (evidence, for Referee B): the mathematical conclusion for k=3..12 (and 13) is conditional on the stage-A enumeration actually producing zero survivors for k ≤ 12 and exactly the one listed tuple at k=13; the orchestrator's re-run of code_1 timed out (its default argument range is 3..16, where k ≥ 14 does not finish), and the re-runs of code_2/code_3 were invoked without the required arguments, so the trusted observations neither confirm nor contradict the reported counts. Reporting caveat: for k=14,15,16 the submission honestly reports 'unfinished, not claimed' but does not give the node counts reached, which the hand-in rules ask for in a partial search; this is a completeness-of-report issue, not a mathematical error, and nothing is claimed for those sizes.
